# browser-image-metadata capability matrix

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-capabilities.mjs from scripts/capabilities-manifest.json; manifest-sha256: f8631decde6b4a1daee843b2375848bc99039d3cc24b507d5e87f9838ebc7300 -->

This matrix describes the `browser-image-metadata` 2.0 alpha surface. It is generated from the checked-in capability manifest and is intentionally narrower than format detection: a container can be recognized even when a particular metadata family or modification is not implemented.

Detection is signature recognition only. A detected format does not imply that every metadata family, read scope, redaction target, or rewrite operation is supported.

| Container | Read | Selective decode | JPEG header Blob read | Metadata-only Blob/File read | Lossless removal | Strict sanitization |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JPEG | Dimensions and image details, EXIF, XMP, IPTC-IIM, decoded common ICC tags, JFIF | EXIF tags and metadata groups | Yes | Yes | EXIF, XMP, IPTC, ICC, JFIF, recognized EXIF fields | Yes, subject to the reported outcome and inspection gaps |
| PNG | Dimensions and image details, EXIF, XMP, decoded common ICC tags, text chunks | EXIF and metadata groups | No | Yes | EXIF, XMP, ICC, PNG text; W04 metadata writing | Yes, subject to the reported outcome |
| TIFF / BigTIFF | Dimensions and image details, EXIF, XMP, IPTC-IIM, decoded common ICC tags | EXIF tags and metadata groups | No | Yes (classic TIFF and BigTIFF) | No | No |
| WebP | Dimensions and image details, EXIF, XMP, decoded common ICC tags | EXIF and metadata groups | No | Yes | EXIF, XMP, ICC; W05 metadata writing | Yes, subject to the reported outcome |
| GIF | Dimensions and image details, comments, animation loop data, XMP application extensions | XMP only | No | No | No | No |
| JPEG XL | Codestream/container dimensions, EXIF, and XMP from JPEG XL boxes | EXIF and metadata groups | No | No | No | No |
| HEIF | Primary dimensions, bounded HEIF item graphs, ISO-BMFF sequence tracks/samples, EXIF, XMP, decoded common ICC tags, transforms, nclx | EXIF tags and metadata groups | No | Yes | No | No |
| AVIF | Primary dimensions, bounded AVIF item graphs, ISO-BMFF sequence tracks/samples, EXIF, XMP, decoded common ICC tags, transforms, nclx | EXIF tags and metadata groups | No | Yes | No | No |

`selectiveDecode` means the reader avoids decoding unrequested EXIF fields and metadata families where that container supports selection. A `Yes` or partial scope is still bounded by the parser's limits and may fall back to a full read for unsupported or malformed layouts.

`jpegHeaderBlobRead` and `metadataBlobFileRead` describe Blob/File range behavior. Partial reads report `completeness.scope`, `bytesRead`, `inputBytes`, and machine-readable `coverage.reasons`.

Every affirmative matrix cell carries positive, malformed, and selection evidence in the manifest. The capability contract test validates that evidence remains present when a claim is changed.

## Output adapters

Lossless adapters: `toJsonSafeResult()`, `toLosslessFamilyGroups()`, `queryMetadata()`, `queryStructuredXmp()`, `queryImageDetails()`, `queryIptcSemantic()`, `queryIccTags()`. Migration adapters: `toFlatObject()`, `toFamilyGroups()`, `toExifReaderCompatible()`, `toExifrCompatible()`. The default duplicate policy is `preserve`; browser thumbnail URLs are exported from `browser-image-metadata/browser-thumbnail` and require explicit idempotent revocation.

Adapter budgets default to 8,192 items and 4 MiB of retained output. Callers can tighten these limits; truncation is explicit and never silently presented as complete.

## Removal semantics

Removal and W03 JPEG writing copy encoded image payloads without recompressing pixels. JPEG entropy-coded scan data, PNG IDAT data, and WebP image chunks remain encoded as they were. W03 writes JPEG EXIF, standard/Extended XMP, ICC, and IPTC marker metadata while preserving scans and decoding-critical markers; JPEGs with MPF secondary images, Ultra HDR gain-map XMP, JUMBF/C2PA, or other protected offset-bearing structures are refused atomically.

`redactMetadata()` reports every operation through `outcome`. A successful outcome means every requested target that is supported for the detected format was handled; it does not mean unknown container data has been interpreted. `auditPrivacy()` identifies recognized sensitive values, opaque blocks, thumbnails, trailing data, warnings, and inspection gaps before a sharing workflow makes a policy decision.

`sanitizeMetadata()` is the strict sharing API. It preserves ICC information and EXIF orientation by default, removes recognized descriptive metadata, and returns bytes only when the policy has been satisfied. Callers must check both `successful` and `data`.

```ts
const result = await sanitizeMetadata(file);
if (result.successful && result.data !== null) await share(result.data);
else showReasons(result.reasons);
```

## Input and runtime support

The public input type is `ArrayBuffer`, any `ArrayBufferView`, `Blob`, or `File`. The core parser does not fetch URLs, paths, or network resources. The separate `browser-image-metadata/fetch` entry point provides opt-in, input-bounded response streaming for browser and compatible runtime fetch implementations.

The published package includes ESM, CommonJS, source maps, declarations, focused detection/fetch/http/node/JPEG/redaction/XMP/worker entry points, and a dependency-free core. Node.js 22 or newer is covered in CI; browser, worker, Node, and Deno usage examples are included.

## Explicit limitations

- Detection is signature recognition only; it is not a claim that every metadata family is supported.
- Partial Blob/File scopes report completeness.scope, bytesRead, inputBytes, and coverage reasons.
- The browser-image-metadata/http entry point performs explicit HTTP range metadata reads. It validates Content-Range, identity encoding, total size, validators, redirects, and caller-selected origins; it fails closed unless allowFullResponseFallback permits a bounded full response. result.telemetry.http records request, response, decoded-byte, cache, fallback, redirect, validator, and completeness evidence.
- The browser-image-metadata/node entry is Node-only: paths, FileHandles, and seekable file sources use the existing bounded range planners, while non-seekable binary streams are fully spooled under maxInputBytes and cannot provide true range efficiency. File descriptors and owned sources close by default on success, failure, and abort; closeSource:false makes external ownership explicit.
- Unsupported and malformed structures remain visible through capabilities, coverage, warnings, and explicit redaction outcomes.
- W01 `editMetadata()` validates canonical-field and explicit-selector transactions, preserve-first policies, bounded values, and typed operation evidence. W02 executes exact EXIF field set/delete/copy/alias/rename transactions for standalone classic TIFF and BigTIFF through the reusable graph serializer with fixed-point verification. W03 executes transactional JPEG marker metadata writing for EXIF, standard/Extended XMP, ICC, and IPTC while preserving entropy scans and decoding-critical markers. W04 executes transactional PNG eXIf, XMP, text, and ICC chunk writing while preserving IDAT and APNG image payloads. W05 executes selective WebP EXIF field and XMP/ICC writing while preserving VP8/VP8L/ALPH/ANMF image payloads; other container writers remain explicit unsupported results. W06 adds deterministic RDF/XML and IPTC-IIM serializers, explicit conflict policies, and deterministic Extended XMP chunk generation while retaining raw/lexical values and unknown properties. W07 adds registry-backed typed redaction selectors for field, family, sensitivity, URI/local-name, block, and associated-image identity, with atomic preflight rejection, physical duplicate-block scoping, and machine-based outcomes. W08 adds an independent public verifier for encoded image-payload ranges, dimensions, image relationships, configured color/orientation policies, and explicit non-pixel-equivalence evidence.
- The public npm brand and import name are browser-image-metadata; image-metadata-toolkit is the repository slug only.
- IPTC Photo Metadata 2025.1 semantics are additive through iptcSemantic/readIptcSemantic; all IIM and URI-aware XMP candidates and conflicts remain available, while unknown XMP remains conservatively classified.
- T01 auditPrivacy() performs bounded semantic privacy inspection for decoded EXIF/IPTC/XMP values and opaque structures. Findings expose stable state/category/reason identifiers, exact provenance links where available, and omit raw values unless includeRawValues is explicitly enabled.
- T02 exposes immutable versioned share-safe, location-safe, anonymous, retain-rights, publisher, accessibility, and forensic-preserve policy presets. Strict policy sanitization refuses output when coverage or exact-field targeting is insufficient; policy reports include the exact ID and version.
- T03 inventoryC2pa()/inventoryJumbfC2pa() structurally inventory C2PA/JUMBF carrier ranges in JPEG, PNG, WebP, and ISO-BMFF without cryptographic verification or remote fetches. Applicable writers refuse detected C2PA-bearing input by default unless an explicit mutation policy is selected.
- T04 is an optional integration layer exposed only from browser-image-metadata/c2pa/browser and browser-image-metadata/c2pa/node. Exact optional official SDK peers are isolated from core bundles; npm run test:c2pa runs the pinned real browser and Node adapters and retains redistribution-safe evidence in reports/c2pa-adapter-integration.{json,md}.
- B01 parses JPEG XL codestream and container dimensions, complete and partial codestream boxes, and bounded uncompressed or Brotli-compressed Exif/XML metadata. Raw codestream metadata is not inferred as container metadata; Brotli support is explicit through an injected decoder or the runtime platform stream.
- B02 exposes bounded HEIF/AVIF item graphs through result.heif: iloc construction methods 0, 1, and 2, multiple extents, self-contained data references, ordered thmb/auxl/dimg/cdsc/iloc relationships, ispe/auxC/irot/imir/colr properties, and grid/iovl/iden derived descriptors. It never decodes pixels or dereferences external data references; malformed, cyclic, unsupported, or over-limit structures remain typed diagnostics. Blob/File metadata scope uses the same bounded method-aware resolver and falls back to a full read when the layout cannot be reconstructed safely.
- ICC inspection decodes bounded ASCII/legacy descriptions, text, MLUC, XYZ, sampled and parametric curves, matrices, measurement, viewing-condition, colorant, signature, and LUT8/LUT16/A-to-B/B-to-A header structures. Exact shared payload ranges are accepted, partial overlaps are rejected, and unknown payloads remain range-only; color transforms are never applied. `npm run icc:reference` requires the complete hash-pinned corpus in `data/icc/reference-corpus.json`, compares the standards-based decoder with pinned ExifTool 13.42 output, records semantic matches and explicit non-comparable values, and fails on incomplete or mismatching evidence. The checked redistribution-safe reports are `reports/icc-reference-report.json` and `reports/icc-reference-report.md`.
- MakerNote interpretation and PNG/WebP/HEIF/AVIF writing remain unsupported. B02 exposes bounded HEIF/AVIF item and relationship semantics and B03 exposes bounded HEIF/AVIF sequence tracks, samples, timing, transformations, associations, and explicit primary-track ambiguity without decoding pixels. W02 writes standalone classic TIFF and BigTIFF EXIF graphs in both byte orders; W03 writes bounded JPEG marker metadata with explicit fail-closed boundaries.
- EXIF date strings do not imply a timezone unless a separate offset tag exists.
